subtopics.title: Composition and Necessity of the Public Sector

questions.question: Water supply, refuse removal and municipal streets are the responsibility of:
options: Local government — the municipalities
National government
The Reserve Bank
State-owned enterprises

questions.question: A public good is NON-RIVALROUS and NON-EXCLUDABLE, meaning:
options: It is free to produce and free to sell
One person's use subtracts nothing from anyone else's, and non-payers cannot be kept out
Only government employees may use it
It is rationed by price

questions.question: No private seller can bill for a patrolled, safe street because of:
options: Municipal by-laws
The parastatal problem
The free-rider problem — since non-payers cannot be excluded, everyone waits for everyone else to pay
The Laffer curve

questions.question: Government taxes alcohol and tobacco but subsidises basic education and immunisation because:
options: Education is cheaper to provide
Alcohol earns no revenue
Both sets of goods are public goods
Markets over-supply demerit goods with harmful spillovers and under-supply merit goods whose benefits overflow the buyer

subtopics.title: Problems of Provisioning and the Objectives of the Public Sector

questions.question: Accountability is weak in public provisioning because:
options: The wire connecting payment to service is cut — officials spend money that is not theirs, and voters get a say only once in five years
Auditors check the accounts too often
Taxpayers choose which services to fund
Public servants face daily customer discipline

questions.question: Without a competitor or profit test, waste in a department often goes unpunished because:
options: Departments are always efficient
There is no automatic penalty — and a department that exhausts its budget is frequently granted a bigger one
The auditor-general sets the budget
Competition law forbids penalties

questions.question: The PARASTATAL problem, visible in Eskom's debt and load-shedding, is that state enterprises:
options: Have no employees
Are barred from selling their output
Must trade commercially while carrying social mandates no business would volunteer for, and the strain shows
Belong to foreign governments

questions.question: The five macroeconomic objectives of the public sector are:
options: Privatisation, taxation, borrowing, spending and auditing
Free water, free electricity, free housing, free transport and free data
Higher tariffs, lower wages, weaker rand, more gold and fewer imports
Economic growth, full employment, price stability, exchange-rate stability and economic equity

subtopics.title: The Budget, Fiscal Policy and the Laffer Curve

questions.question: Sorted DIRECT versus INDIRECT, the taxes are:
options: Direct: personal and company tax on income; indirect: VAT and excise on spending
Direct: VAT; indirect: personal income tax
Direct: customs duties; indirect: company tax
All South African taxes are direct

questions.question: Maize meal, brown bread and rice are zero-rated for VAT because:
options: They are luxury goods
VAT is regressive in effect — poorer households spend a larger share of income, so zero-rating pulls their essential basket out of the net
They cannot be taxed administratively
Farmers refuse to charge VAT

questions.question: A STRUCTURAL deficit is one that:
options: Appears only in a downswing
Occurs when revenue exceeds spending
Persists through every phase of the cycle — the reason debt-service costs now compete with classrooms for the same rand
Is financed by printing money

questions.question: On the Laffer curve, revenue is zero at both a rate of 0 percent and 100 percent because:
options: The curve only applies to VAT
Revenue never varies with the rate
Government chooses not to collect at those rates
At zero nothing is charged, and at one hundred percent nobody will work or declare income that is confiscated whole

questions.question: PUBLIC SECTOR FAILURE is defined as:
options: Government intervention allocating resources less efficiently than the market it meant to improve on
Any budget deficit
The existence of taxes
A market failing to supply public goods

questions.question: Which list contains CAUSES of public sector failure?
options: Non-rivalry, non-excludability and externalities
Management failure, apathy, bureaucracy, politics overriding economics, and corruption
Growth, equity and stability
Zero-rating, excise and customs

questions.question: Failing public services hurt the poor most because:
options: The poor pay most of the company tax
Grants rise when services fail
The wealthy exit into private schools, clinics and security, while the poor cannot buy substitutes
The poor use no public services

questions.question: The balanced conclusion the long essay rewards is:
options: The state should own all firms
Markets never fail, only states do
Neither failure has a remedy
Market failure justifies the public sector and public sector failure disciplines it — judge which failure is worse in the case at hand and name the correction for each

subtopics.title: What the Street Cannot Buy for Itself

questions.question: The vetkoek, the data bundle and the haircut belong in the private-goods pile because:
options: The seller can turn non-payers away — pay and it is yours
Government subsidises them
They are non-excludable
Everyone consumes them equally

questions.question: The night patrol never starts without government because:
options: Patrolling is illegal for private citizens
Every household waits for the neighbours to pay, since nobody can be excluded from the safety once the patrol walks
The street has no crime
The patrol requires special equipment

questions.question: The clinic sits on the middle shelf between private goods and public goods because:
options: It cannot legally charge fees
It is non-rivalrous like the patrol
It could sell its services, but one child's immunisation shields the whole street, so the market alone buys too little of it
Its services are demerit goods

questions.question: The grant on the second of the month represents:
options: Payment for labour supplied to the state
A loan from the municipality
An indirect tax refund
Redistribution — correcting the market, which pays what labour fetches rather than what a household needs

subtopics.title: Why the Tap Runs Slow — the Trouble with Providing

questions.question: The chicken shop stays sharp while the housing office often does not because:
options: The shop faces a daily election — dry chicken today, empty till tomorrow — while the office's clients cannot go elsewhere and its budget arrives regardless
Chicken is easier to manage than housing
The office has better equipment
Officials are lazier people than cooks

questions.question: The housing department cannot plan like the chicken shop because:
options: It has too many staff
No price tells it how many houses or nurses are needed — it must guess through censuses, surveys and councillors' promises
Demand for houses does not exist
Its budget is too large to spend

questions.question: The stepped electricity tariff — free basic units, then dearer blocks — solves the pricing puzzle by:
options: Charging everyone full cost from the first unit
Making all electricity free
Making necessity free while charging luxury use dearly, so a pensioner can boil a kettle and the substation still gets funded
Handing pricing to a private monopoly

questions.question: "Serve the villages and the balance sheet haemorrhages; serve the balance sheet and the villages stay dark" describes:
options: The free-rider problem
Progressive taxation
The Laffer curve
The parastatal tension — a state enterprise pulled between commercial survival and social mandates

subtopics.title: February's Envelope and the Tax That Bites Back

questions.question: The biggest single stream INTO February's envelope is:
options: Income tax off the country's payslips
Customs duties
Sales of gold reserves
Donations from abroad

questions.question: Borrowing every year merely to cover salaries and interest is dangerous because:
options: All borrowing is forbidden
This year's classroom is paid for by a future taxpayer, while interest grows into one of the fastest-rising lines in the budget
It automatically strengthens the rand
Ports can only be built with tax money

questions.question: In the barber's story, pushing the tax rate past the crest means:
options: Revenue rises without limit
The barber pays happily
Each extra percentage point collects LESS, as people work fewer hours, hide sales or melt into the informal economy
VAT must be abolished

questions.question: The evaluation sentence on the Laffer curve is:
options: The curve proves all taxes should be cut
Revenue peaks at one hundred percent
The curve applies only to barbers
Nobody can say where the crest sits — the curve warns against overreach, it does not issue instructions
